clips.title: The story
paras: Camping 101: Skinning instructs adventurers in turning harvested pelts into a functional Camp Chair for field camps. Guided by Mendalass Tattermend in Shen'dar Village, skinners learn to combine their harvesting craft with wilderness survival and campfire relaxation.

Harvesting hides from fallen beasts is an essential survival skill across Azeroth, but its utility extends far beyond simple armor crafting. Through Camping 101: Skinning, gatherers learn to direct their trade toward wilderness survival by crafting a portable Camp Chair. Taking time to rest upon a comfortable seat out in the wilds allows weary adventurers to regain their strength and remain in peak fighting condition before their next battle.

To master this pattern, adventurers are sent to Shen'dar Village to meet with Mendalass Tattermend once they have proven their proficiency with a skinning knife. Mendalass instructs travelers on assembling durable seating from collected pelts. However, establishing a campsite requires more than just furniture: settlements will not tolerate impromptu camps within town limits, and no site is truly finished without a crackling campfire, a skill traditionally picked up from local culinary instructors.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: Being able to skillfully harvest the skins and hides of fallen beasts is one of the more valuable skills an adventurer can possess.

I reckon I know someone that can teach you how to craft a Camp Chair for your camp. Sometimes it's important to just take a load off, and you can use some of those hides you've gathered to make a comfy chair to sit in. A bit of relaxation can help ensure that you are at your peak condition and can strike where it counts the next time you find yourself in a dust-up.

clips.title: Completion
paras: There you have it, you can now craft your very own Camp Chair. Most folk don't care much for camps being set up in the center of town, so you'll need to head into the wilderness if you want to test it out.

Oh, and just remember, no camp is complete without a campfire. You'll need one of those before you start up your camp. Most cooks can teach you to make a fire. If you haven't already, you might want to check in with someone who can train you in the culinary arts to learn the basics.
